summary: You were in the hospital because your lung disease flared up and you had pneumonia. Your heart was also holding on to extra fluid, so it was hard to breathe. You are going home with steroid pills, an antibiotic, and a higher dose of your water pill. Finish the prednisone and the doxycycline. Use your inhalers the right way and weigh yourself every day.

diagnoses.plain: A flare-up of your long-term lung disease (COPD)
Weak heart that held on to extra fluid (heart failure)
diagnoses.clinical: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure

diagnoses.plain: Low oxygen that needed extra oxygen, now better

new.name: Prednisone
new.howOften: once a day by mouth for 2 more days
new.why: A steroid pill that calms the swelling in your lungs. Take both remaining days.

new.name: Doxycycline
new.howOften: twice a day by mouth for 3 more days
new.why: An antibiotic to finish treating the pneumonia. Take every dose.

new.name: Furosemide
new.why: Your water pill at a higher dose than before. It takes extra fluid off so you breathe easier. You will urinate more.

continue.name: Maintenance inhaler
continue.why: Keeps your airways open. Use it every day even when you feel fine.

continue.name: Rescue albuterol inhaler
continue.howOften: as needed when breathing gets hard
continue.why: Opens your airways fast during a bad spell.

continue.name: Carvedilol
continue.howOften: at the dose on your discharge list
continue.why: Helps your heart and blood pressure.

stop.name: Previous lower-dose furosemide regimen
stop.why: Stopped. The new 40 mg dose replaces it. Do not take both.

stop.name: Any duplicate inhaler therapy
stop.why: Stopped. Use only the inhalers on your final medication list so you do not double up.

checklist.text: Take Prednisone 40 mg once a day for 2 more days
Take Doxycycline 100 mg twice a day for 3 more days
Take Furosemide 40 mg once a day (the new, higher dose)
Use your maintenance inhaler every day; use the rescue inhaler only when breathing gets hard
Weigh yourself every day and write it down
Use your home oxygen at the flow rate and times you were prescribed
Stop smoking. Ask your care team for help and resources

call911: Severe shortness of breath that your rescue inhaler does not help
Blue or gray lips, or you cannot speak because you are so breathless
New confusion or you cannot stay awake
goToER: You need much more oxygen than usual
High fever or a cough that quickly gets worse with more phlegm
Fast weight gain with more swelling or trouble breathing when lying flat
callClinic: You are using the rescue inhaler more than usual
You are not sure which inhaler to use or how to use it

followUps.why: Check your recovery and your medicines
Check your COPD plan, inhalers and oxygen
Check your heart failure and the furosemide dose

questionsToAsk: Can you watch me use my inhalers to make sure I am doing it right?
What oxygen flow rate should I use, and when?
How much weight gain should make me call you?
What programs can help me quit smoking?
What should I do if I run out of prednisone or doxycycline early?
